resolved_source_locations.conclusion: The anti-relabeling ledger is part of the result. This paper does not claim the predictive-state or causal-state quotient construction as new; that is a standard way to summarize a process by its predictive consequences . It does not claim the closure-deficit identity, or the optimality of the best autonomous macro-predictor, as new; those are imported from the closure-deficit and no-go accounts . It does not claim the strict-extension, saturation, or promotion-obligation framework as new; those are imported standards for recognizing when a higher vocabulary is a genuine layer rather than a relabeling . Nor does it claim as new the game-theoretic fact that added structure matters. Folk theorems show that repeated interaction can support many outcomes; global games show how noisy private information can select; reputation models show how type structure changes play; evolutionary and stochastic-stability models show that convention selection can be a property of a run; correlated equilibrium and type spaces show how signals and hidden state enlarge the game . These are reference points the paper uses, not results it rebrands. The contribution is the conjunction, on one explicit repeated-game object, under one evidentiary discipline. First, the paper installs the predictive state as the canonical institution of repeated play and verifies, on the finite carrier, that it is not definable from the game's own stage vocabulary: the institutional partition strictly refines the stage partition and does not factor through it. Second, the paper prices the omission exactly by closure deficit, with a gap–residual decomposition that separates what conditioning on the institution recovers from what remains unpredictable even after that conditioning. Third, it assembles these facts into a certified strict-extension object: the institutional vocabulary saturates, admits an active label-feedback exhibit under a declared extension, and passes the admissibility gates for a promoted layer on the carrier. Fourth, the picture is subjected to tests that could have failed silently but were reported in full: the run-layer constants are reproducible within protocol yet fail three frozen out-of-sample transfer attempts, and the human-data analysis confirms the predictive-residue hypothesis while reversing the proposed timing bridge. The registered negatives are not qualifications to the result; they are part of the evidence for the strict-extension reading.

resolved_source_locations.conclusion: Formal theories of consciousness are difficult to compare, and difficult to trust, partly because three different kinds of claim routinely travel in one sentence: mathematical claims about a formal structure, empirical claims about how that structure meets observation, and ontological claims about what the structure's satisfaction would be. The field has begun to treat this as a foundational problem rather than a stylistic one. General frameworks for mathematical models of consciousness ask what a model must declare before it says anything ; formal work on testability shows that inference procedures and prediction data can interact so badly that a theory becomes unfalsifiable or trivially falsified ; and large adversarial collaborations have demonstrated how much machinery is needed to test even two well-resourced theories against each other, without producing a definitive verdict . Landscape reviews count theory families by the dozen . In such a field, a paper's first obligation is to say exactly what kind of claim each of its sentences makes. This paper takes that obligation as its organizing principle. It presents an architecture for consciousness built from standard finite mathematics: finite carriers, lenses, quotients, refinements, closure operators, viability kernels, and audited promotion between description layers. Around that architecture it assembles a catalog of exact finite results, a small set of machine-checked kernels, and one explicitly priced ontological bridge. Every scientific sentence in the paper is assigned to one of four claim lanes, defined in Section : structural results [S] (theorems and exact finite constructions), recognition bridges [R] (proposed interpretive mappings, never derivations), ontological implications [O] (conditional on named postulates), and open targets [OPEN] . The lane discipline is not decoration; it is enforced by a sentence-level claim ledger in the artifact, and the paper's central negative rule is that no amount of [S] material ever implies an [O] conclusion without the named purchases.

resolved_source_locations.conclusion: We propose that to be real is to have closed: that reality is not a substance, a substrate, or a set, but a ledger of survived closures. A thing is real when it is a package that earned its objecthood through audited gates and pays, continuously, to keep it. The proposal is grounded in the Six Birds corpus, which has spent the last years doing something Nietzsche predicted and no one else has attempted: worshipping the stone. The corpus constructs geometry, logic, time, probability, objects, events, agents, institutions, and selves from bare substrates, under explicit audit, with every failure banked and every success priced. The method of this paper is an itemized metaphysics. Every claim is either free, a theorem of the corpus at its stated grade, or purchased, spending one of two named axioms: Ontic Closure Completeness and Substrate Indifference. On this basis we argue that the Born rule's shape is the generic fate of compressed record layers, so that probability is born at the lens; that a simulation which passes a closure's gates is not a simulation of the thing but an instance of it, which is why lattice QCD computes the true proton; that ``matter'' and ``information'' are altitude labels, so that an economy is literally a ghost made of people; that mathematics is closure engineering in vitro, the design of lawful theory extensions ahead of any run, and in practice a map that unfolds only where someone walks; that the explanatory gap of consciousness is a non-descent certificate, predicted rather than embarrassing; that life and intelligence are graded, auditable positions on real axes rather than binaries; that a civilization which learns this grammar crosses into the era of meta-emergence, where creation itself is a wielded power, and that peace is a closure state, an achievement that strengthens rather than dissolves the identities it comprises; and that the great paradoxes (sorites, Theseus, Zeno, Mary's room, the unreasonable effectiveness of mathematics, the arrow of time) dissolve under ledger discipline, most of them because they demanded of a layer a certificate that no layer can issue. We close eight old problems and open eight new ones. The last sacrifice is Sacrifice itself.

resolved_source_locations.conclusion: A certificate, in the sense used here, is a finite package of obligations and evidence. It is meant to prevent a higher-level object from being accepted merely because it has been renamed. The imported strict-extension framework specifies the obligations for certifying that a higher vocabulary is a genuine strict extension of a lower one . For the repeated-game setting, the relevant obligations are: a closed base law for the lower layer, meaning the best autonomous predictor available in the stage vocabulary; saturation of the higher vocabulary, meaning a predictive refinement fixed point; non-factorization, witnessed by split pairs whose distinctions are not definable from below; an exact quantitative price for omitting the higher layer, given by positive closure deficit and the gap–residual decomposition; material forcing, when a declared extension lets the higher layer feed back into play; and admissibility of the promoted object, checked by the gate battery described in . [Strict-extension certificate on the declared carrier] On the declared finite carrier, the canonical institutional state M=P_ is a certified strict extension of the stage game. The closed base law and exact price are supplied by ; non-factorization is supplied by ; saturation is supplied by ; material forcing is supplied, relative to its declared label-feedback extension, by ; and admissibility is supplied by the promotion certificate .

resolved_source_locations.conclusion: Twelve limitations, before any conclusion. Exact finite models only. Every positive result lives on a declared toy carrier. Nothing licenses transfer to large, noisy, or continuous systems beyond the displayed conditional schemas. No empirical content. No dataset, no parameter fit, no validation, no phenomenon rows (Section ). Provenance of predictions. The artifact contains documents labelled as predictions, but their initial Git history does not establish temporal precedence over implementations, and later corrections are versioned. Nothing in this paper calls them preregistered. Selected mechanization. Lean coverage is selected, not catalog-wide: kernels prove core facts and pin many enumerated values as certified constants matching the Python computations (per-law boundaries in Table and Appendix ); the current manifest-level validator accepts a zero-row schema and is a known release blocker, so no manifest-audited coverage claim is made. Inherited trust base. The Lean development trusts vendored foundations modules and declared axioms from the companion corpus, cataloged in Appendix ; their opacity guards are inherited, not re-proved. T1's family boundary. The forcing theorem is exact on one carrier; the family schema's hypotheses (live non-definable phase, deadline relevance) are strong and not claimed common (Section ). T12's open target. Geometry birth (fitted distortion, dimension, curvature transport) is not landed; the landed object is an audited induced geometry. T16's conventions. The meta-problem composition is relative to a declared completion convention, and its carrier collapses several premises extensionally. T17's open core. The simplified/full schema relation is unproved in both directions, certificate soundness is assumed where used, A2 has no formal theorem, and T17-I, the integrated instance, is open (Section ). T18c demoted. The temporal-precondition claim is a dependency observation, not a theorem. Recognition bridges are unproved. Valence, phenomenological clause mappings, attention readings, and all state-taxonomy readings are named hypotheses ( [R] ), each retractable without structural loss. Review status. The artifact's ``external review request'' documents record an internal author-driven review loop; they are not independent peer review, and this preprint has not been peer reviewed.

resolved_source_locations.conclusion: The exact results in this paper live on a specific finite carrier: a memory-one reactive-rule catalog, two main payoff families, a uniform prior, and declared lenses, rounds, horizons, and extensions. Their highest grade is theorem-grade-on-the-carrier, not a general repeated-game theorem. The run constants are scoped to the declared payoff families, evolutionary dynamics, population sizes, noise grids, estimators, and protocols. The no-shortcut conclusion is correspondingly scoped to the tested formula classes and the three frozen transfer tests; it is not a proof that no transferable shortcut exists. The human-data analysis is one published dataset analyzed under one frozen protocol, with mapping amendments recorded before analysis; it does not confirm or refute any carrier theorem. The broader framework results used here, including predictive quotients, closure deficit, strict-extension obligations, and promotion gates, are imported and cited , not re-proved. Finally, the material-forcing result is relative to its declared label-feedback extension; it is not a claim that institutional labels generally enrich play.

resolved_source_locations.conclusion: The most direct next construction is a within-agent learning or acquisition carrier, in which the individual agent is treated as a carrier object in the sense of the Six Birds treatment of agency . The failed crystallization bridge in shows that experience-as-composition selection makes the finite carrier more homogeneous and more stage-predictable, whereas the data show history-dependence growing with experience. A carrier in which individual agents acquire conditional rules over their own histories would test the mechanism that this contrast leaves open. A second direction is a broader family of noisy and dissipative carriers, to map route memory beyond the tested noise grid and to learn when currentizable traces become genuinely coherent. A third is to enlarge the strategic and payoff substrate: richer automata, larger action spaces, asymmetric games, and longer public signals would test which carrier facts persist and which are artifacts of the minimal catalog. The run layer also invites a bounded-rationality connection. The imitation dynamics used here contain a logit-style temperature parameter; in a maximum-entropy or shadow-price reading, such a parameter can be interpreted as the dual of a binding cognitive or informational budget rather than a free behavioral knob . That connection is only an opening in this paper, but it suggests how run-only constants might be tied to explicit resource constraints. On the empirical side, the immediate extension is broader pre-registered testing of the residue hypothesis and the timing reversal on other repeated-game datasets, with the same discipline: hypotheses, predictors, bands, folds, and amendments fixed before outcome analysis.
